shorts.title: Hochul Signs Up For Trump's School Choice Plan, Unions Fume #Shorts
shorts.hook: "I'm not going to leave money on the table"
shorts.narration: [amused] Folks, Kathy Hochul just signed New York up for a Trump program. [beat] Somebody check her temperature. [serious] On Friday, New York's Democratic governor opted the state into the federal scholarship tax credit from Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill. Teachers unions and their allies had pushed her to say no. Her answer: "I'm not going to leave money on the table when it could help our kids." [beat] Friends, when even Albany smells free money, you know it's good money. [sarcastic] Teachers union president Michael Mulgrew called it "a failure of leadership." [beat] Michael, from a union boss, that's practically a thank-you card. [warm] Proverbs 22:6 says, "Train up a child in the way he should go." Letting parents pick that way? That's the whole idea. [mischievously] So, Democrats: is Hochul a Trump convert, or just counting votes before November? Tell me below, and subscribe, because Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: On Friday, Oct. 9, 2026, Gov. Kathy Hochul opted New York into the federal scholarship tax credit; she is the second Democratic governor to opt in voluntarily.
The credit passed in 2025 as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which President Trump backed.
A coalition of teachers unions and other public school advocates petitioned Hochul to reject the program.
Hochul said: "I'm not going to leave money on the table when it could help our kids."
United Federation of Teachers President Michael Mulgrew called the decision "a failure of leadership."
Hochul is running for reelection in November.

shorts.title: Trump Fires Back At Nobel Committee: 'We Will Not Forget, Norway' #Shorts
shorts.narration: [emphatic] Folks, Norway handed out its Peace Prize, and President Trump had some thoughts. [serious] On Friday, the Nobel Peace Prize went to South African jurist Navi Pillay, a former U.N. human rights chief. That same day, at a rally in Syracuse, Trump called the award "an indelible stain on the country of Norway." [beat] Somewhere in Oslo, a committee member is hiding behind a herring barrel. [incredulous] Trump said the prize "has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy." Then: "we will not forget, Norway." [beat] [deadpan] Friends, in Norway that's scarier than a winter with no coffee. [warm] Ecclesiastes 1:9 says, "there is no new thing under the sun." [beat] A Nobel committee passing over Trump? The Preacher saw that rerun coming. [mischievously] So, should Oslo say sorry, or should Trump just build a bigger trophy? Comments below, and subscribe, because Henry roasts the news every day.

shorts.title: Susan Collins To Debate Rival: 'You Owe Me An Apology' #Shorts
shorts.narration: [incredulous] Folks, Maine's Senate debate got hotter than a lobster pot. [serious] Thursday night, Democratic challenger Troy Jackson accused Republican Senator Susan Collins and her husband of profiting from the Iran war. His words: "She could use her leverage to stop the war, but instead they are making money." [beat] Bold strategy, friends: accuse first, let the fact-checkers sort it out later. [emphatic] Collins shot back: "That is absolutely outrageous, and you owe me an apology." [deadpan] Jackson didn't back down. [beat] He only stepped in to replace Graham Platner less than three months ago, and he's already skipped the chapter on manners. [warm] Proverbs 18:17 says, "He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him." [mischievously] And that was debate two of four in ten days. [beat] Maine, stock up on popcorn. So, should Jackson apologize? Tell me below, and subscribe, because Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: Sen. Susan Collins and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson met Thursday night for their second debate, hosted by WMTW; it was the second of four debates in 10 days.
Jackson accused Collins and her husband of profiting from the war with Iran.
Jackson said: "She could use her leverage to stop the war, but instead they are making money."
Collins said: "That is absolutely outrageous, and you owe me an apology."
Collins is a Republican; Jackson did not retreat from the accusation.
Jackson stepped in less than three months ago to replace Graham Platner.
